janet (customer): Hi team — we're getting 401s from the Redwood API suddenly. Error body: {\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"API key invalid\"}}. Happening since this morning after a scheduled rotation. Using curl from our CI container.

Ava (Support): sorry you're hitting that, janet. Can you paste the curl you used (sanitized) and the request id from the response headers if present? Also which SDK or direct curl?

janet (customer): curl we run in CI: ```
curl -s -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input":"test"}' 
  https://api.redwoodinference.example/v1/generate
```
Response headers include `x-redwood-request-id: rwd-7f3a9c`. The key was rotated in our secrets manager around 06:10 UTC. CI job runs at 06:15 and started failing. Manual `curl` from laptop with the same secret returns 401 too.

Ava (Support): thanks. Two quick checks: 1) confirm the value in the CI env actually updated (sometimes old container envs persist), and 2) confirm there isn't any accidental whitespace (newlines/CR) in the key after copy/paste. Can you run `echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | xxd` in CI or locally and paste output?

janet (customer): running now. output: ```
00000000: 4150 495f 4b45 5958 5941 4c32 4d2e 0a     API_KEYXYAL2M..
```
Ah — that `0a` at end looks like a newline. We do rotate keys via our Okta secret sync, maybe it appended a newline.

Liam (Auth Eng): that trailing `0a` (LF) will absolutely break the signature comparison and trigger invalid_api_key. Our header matching is exact. Two remediation options: strip the newline in CI env before usage, or rotate the key again so the stored secret doesn't include newline. Example fix: `export REDWOOD_KEY=$(echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | tr -d '\r\n')`. Also you can use `printf %s "$REDWOOD_KEY"` when storing.

janet (customer): Did that `tr -d` fix it. Re-ran curl: now 200 and response looks good. Thanks.

Ava (Support): great! I'll mark this as resolved once we confirm no other services are still using the old secret. A couple notes for you: 1) CI runners that load secrets at container start may need restart after rotation; 2) some secret-sync scripts (esp. ones that append newline when writing files) will introduce this.

janet (customer): yeah our deploy pipeline was reading from a file and not trimming. We'll update. Would appreciate any docs tips to avoid this going forward.

Liam (Auth Eng): we'll add a short blurb to the docs: recommend `Authorization` header usage `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` or using `-H 'x-api-key: <KEY>'` for non-Bearer flows, and be explicit about trimming whitespace. Also adding SDKs to auto-trim keys before sending is an idea.

Marta (Billing): quick FYI — when customers rotate keys we sometimes see billing spikes if clients keep retrying with invalid keys. Janet, did CI rerun a lot of times? We can discount obvious retry noise if needed.

janet (customer): yes, about 12 retries over ~20 minutes, but looks insignificant. thanks for asking.

Ava (Support): action items: 1) janet will update secret sync to strip newlines; 2) Liam to add note to auth docs + consider SDK auto-trim; 3) Support to close thread after confirmation. Anything else?

janet (customer): no that's all. Appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment rwd/infra-sync completed at 2028-03-04T06:50:00Z :white_check_mark:

Ava (Support): resolving now. If you see anything weird re-open and include `x-redwood-request-id` header value.

Liam (Auth Eng): small follow-up for internal: we should consider making the 401 error message slightly more diagnostic in cases where the key fails due to trailing whitespace — maybe a note in docs rather than exposing internals. Filing a docs task.

janet (customer): filed a quick internal ticket to update the writer job and will ping if anything else shows up. Thanks again!
